mutants.name: drop-dedupe-select
mutants.why: removing the plan-scoped SELECT means record_commits always inserts, so step 2 of a plan gets the shas already recorded under step 1; t1 asserts step 2 returns 1 and holds only c — without the dedupe it returns 3 and holds a, b, c
mutants.anchor:
exists = conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM commits c JOIN steps s ON s.id = c.step_id "
                "WHERE s.plan_id = (SELECT plan_id FROM steps WHERE id = ?) "
                "AND c.repo = ? AND c.sha = ?",
                (step_id, repo, sha),
            ).fetchone()
            if exists:
                continue

mutants.name: drop-first-region-record-commits
mutants.why: removing the record_commits call at the first step-end site means step 1's commits never land under step 1; t7 asserts step 1 has {s1a, s1b} — without this call the set is empty
mutants.anchor:
lifecycle.record_gate_events(_lc_step_id, gate_result)
        lifecycle.record_commits(_lc_step_id, os.path.basename(project_path), _step_commit_shas(wt_path, pre_diff, post_diff))
        _lc_deposits = _build_deposit_records(plan_text, header, project_path, wt_path)

mutants.name: drop-while-loop-record-commits
mutants.why: removing the record_commits call at the while-loop step-end site means step 2's commits never land under step 2 from this site; t7's call_count assertion fires — _step_commit_shas is called 1 time not 2

mutants.name: drop-reverse-flag
mutants.why: removing --reverse from rev-list returns shas newest-first; t4 asserts oldest-first order [sha1, sha2] — without --reverse the order is [sha2, sha1]

mutants.name: flip-range-direction
mutants.why: writing the range as post..pre produces an empty rev-list (no commits are reachable from pre that are not in post); t4 asserts the two new shas are returned — with a flipped range the result is []
